dedupe_keys.name: flooding of the blayais nuclear power plant on 27 december 1999 birraux report to the french parliament 2000

description: This case study covers the flooding of the Blayais nuclear power plant in south-west France on the evening of 27 December 1999, when the tide and the high winds of storm Martin overwhelmed the plant's sea walls on the Gironde estuary. The ETDEWEB record of the report by C. Birraux to the French Parliament, dated 1 July 2000 and written in French, analyses the incidents at the plant and draws lessons on the flood risk of nuclear installations. Wikipedia adds that the plant, with four pressurised water reactors operated by EDF, was designed with a platform 4.5 m above NGF and sea walls of 5.2 m, that the loss of off-site power and several safety systems resulted, and that the event was rated level 2 on INES. Access: the ETDEWEB record gives the abstract and bibliographic data free of charge; the full text is not offered on the page and no licence is stated. Coverage is one site and one event. Caveats: the abstract and an encyclopedia summary were read, not the report; sea wall figures come from the encyclopedia. It suits resilience and post-event analysis studies of coastal nuclear sites, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.

name: Flooding of the Blayais nuclear power plant on 27 December 1999 (Birraux report to the French Parliament, 2000)
outcomes: Storm-driven waves coinciding with high water in the Gironde overtopped the plant's sea walls, flooded the basements of two fuel storage buildings, caused the loss of off-site power and several safety systems, and led to a level 2 rating on the International Nuclear Event Scale; the event changed how flood risk is evaluated at nuclear plants in France.
